newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: PMP dives 7 pct on earnings warning.
newsitem.headline: PMP dives 7 pct on earnings warning.

text.p: Shares in magazines and multi-media group PMP Communications Ltd dived 23 cents or almost seven percent to A$3.17 in early Friday trade after it announced it saw annual earnings falling 15 to 20 percent because of sluggish trading conditions.
PMP is about 45 percent owned by News Corp Ltd.
Some analysts said the price had dived in expectation that PMP, which previously had been seen as a strong dividend/yield stock, would be forced to cut its dividend.
"One of the reasons it has been hit so hard today is traditionally it's been a high yielding stock which people have bought for the dividend stream," said one analyst.
"A lot of those investors are now looking at the shocking second half and seeing it will be very difficult to maintain their dividend," he said.
"They maintained their half year dividend even though earnings were down and it looks like they're not going to be able to pay out the same dividend for the full year."
PMP said on Thursday its pre-tax and abnormals earnings for the year to June 30, 1997 were likely to be 15 percent to 20 percent down on the A$90.38 million posted in 1995/96.
Net profit in 1995/96 fell to A$58.04 million from A$64.44 million in 1994/95.
PMP posted an unchanged final dividend of 10 cents in August 1996, taking its full year dividend to 20.4 cents.
PMP kept its interim dividend for the first half of 1996/97 at 10.4 cents after net profit fell to A$30.55 million from A$31.38 million.
Analysts had on average expected full year 1996/97 net profit before abnornals to be about A$57.9 million, down from the A$62 million posted in 1995/96.
But analysts said this was now likely to be downgraded to about A$50 million.

Some analysts said, however, they were confident PMP could keep its dividend unchanged because of its strong cash flow and that a A$3.17 price represented a strong dividend yield of 6.4 percent given an unchanged dividend.
